title: Special Executive Programme In International Banking Regulations
description: Gain critical insights into the evolving landscape of international banking and global regulatory frameworks.
university: The Global School of Skills (GSS) and Australian University
longDescription: This Special Executive Programme provides an in-depth exploration of international banking, its regulatory aspects, and the impact of globalization on financial markets. Participants will analyze the functions of cross-border banking, foreign exchange markets, and regulatory compliance in a global context.
courseDetails: International financial Markets, Institutions and Regulations. Globalization and Shadow Banking System. Institutions affecting Lending and Banking Regulations. International Agreements regarding Banking and Finance. Bank Regulations its objectives. Basel Accord and Capital Adequacy. General Fund Requirements, US Federal Reserve Bank. Regulations and Supervision. Global Financial Crises its causes and effects. The Post 1970 Development of State Regulation in UK. The Essential Principles for Effective Banking Supervision. Techniques of banking supervision. The European institutional framework for prudential banking supervision. The supervisory review process. Banking Supervision and Compliance. Risk Management and Types of Risks. Corporate Governance and Risk Measurement Techniques for Risk Management Liquidity Risk and Credit Risk E-finance The course covers the evolution, definition, and features of international banking, highlighting the functions of cross-border banking and foreign exchange markets. Regulatory aspects such as international financial institutions, shadow banking, and global banking agreements are examined in detail. Key topics like Basel Accords, capital adequacy, and supervisory frameworks, including European and US regulations, are discussed. Additionally, the programme explores risk management, corporate governance, and current issues affecting global banking operations and compliance. After the successful completion of this course, you will understand the following; International Banking Meaning and Scope: Regulatory aspect of International banking Institutions and Markets: International Banking Regulations: International Banking Supervisions and Compliances: Risks and Current Issues in Global Banking Regulations:

The course covers the evolution, definition, and features of international banking, highlighting the functions of cross-border banking and foreign exchange markets. Regulatory aspects such as international financial institutions, shadow banking, and global banking agreements are examined in detail. Key topics like Basel Accords, capital adequacy, and supervisory frameworks, including European and US regulations, are discussed. Additionally, the programme explores risk management, corporate governance, and current issues affecting global banking operations and compliance.
